slides.title: Welcome to Django
slides.content:
# Django Framework 🎸

Welcome to Django - the web framework for perfectionists with deadlines!

## What you'll learn:
- **What is Django?** - The framework overview
- **Why Django?** - Key advantages
- **Installation** - Setting up Django
- **Project Structure** - Understanding Django's architecture
- **MTV Pattern** - Model, Template, View

## Why Learn Django?
- 🚀 **Rapid Development** - Build apps faster
- 🔒 **Security Built-in** - Protection from common attacks
- 📈 **Scalable** - Powers Instagram, Pinterest, Spotify
- 🔋 **Batteries Included** - Admin panel, ORM, auth out of the box

> 💡 **Fun Fact:** Django was named after the famous jazz guitarist Django Reinhardt. The creators were jazz fans!

Let's build something amazing!

slides.title: What is Django?
slides.content:
# What is Django? 🤔

Django is a **high-level Python web framework** that encourages rapid development and clean, pragmatic design.

## Key Features

```
✅ Object-Relational Mapping (ORM)
✅ URL Routing
✅ Template Engine
✅ Form Handling
✅ Authentication System
✅ Admin Interface
✅ Security Features
✅ Caching
```

## The DRY Principle

**Don't Repeat Yourself** - Django's core philosophy.

```python
# Instead of writing this everywhere:
db_connection = connect()
query = "SELECT * FROM users"
result = db_connection.execute(query)

# Django's ORM:
users = User.objects.all()
```

## Who Uses Django?

- 📸 **Instagram** - Photo sharing
- 📌 **Pinterest** - Visual discovery
- 🎵 **Spotify** - Music streaming (some services)
- 📰 **The Washington Post** - News
- 🔬 **NASA** - Some internal tools

> 🎯 **Django powers over 12,000 of the top 1 million websites!**

slides.title: Advantages of Django
slides.content:
# Why Choose Django? ⭐

## 1. Rapid Development

```python
# Create a complete CRUD app in minutes!
from django.contrib import admin
from .models import Article

admin.site.register(Article)  # Instant admin interface!
```

## 2. Built-in Security

Django protects against:
- 🛡️ **SQL Injection** - ORM handles escaping
- 🛡️ **XSS** - Template auto-escaping
- 🛡️ **CSRF** - Token protection
- 🛡️ **Clickjacking** - X-Frame-Options

## 3. Scalable Architecture

```
Small Blog → Medium App → Enterprise System
     ↓           ↓            ↓
   Django handles all scales!
```

## 4. Batteries Included

| Feature | Django | Other Frameworks |
|---------|--------|------------------|
| Admin Panel | ✅ Built-in | ❌ Add-on |
| Auth System | ✅ Built-in | ❌ Add-on |
| ORM | ✅ Built-in | ❌ Add-on |
| Forms | ✅ Built-in | ❌ Add-on |

## 5. Excellent Documentation

> 💡 **Pro Tip:** Django's docs are legendary! Always check docs.djangoproject.com first.

slides.title: Installing Django
slides.content:
# Installing Django 🔧

## Step 1: Create Virtual Environment

```bash
# Create a virtual environment
python -m venv myenv

# Activate it (Windows)
myenv\Scripts\activate

# Activate it (macOS/Linux)
source myenv/bin/activate
```

## Step 2: Install Django

```bash
# Install latest Django
pip install django

# Install specific version
pip install django==4.2

# Verify installation
python -m django --version
```

## Step 3: Create a Project

```bash
# Create new project
django-admin startproject myproject

# Project structure created:
myproject/
├── manage.py
└── myproject/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── settings.py
    ├── urls.py
    ├── asgi.py
    └── wsgi.py
```

## Step 4: Run Development Server

```bash
cd myproject
python manage.py runserver

# Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ 🎉
```

> ⚠️ **Always use virtual environments!** Never install Django globally.

slides.title: Django Project Structure
slides.content:
# Project Structure 📁

## Project vs App

```
Project = The entire website/application
App = A specific feature (blog, users, shop)

myproject/           # Project
├── manage.py
├── myproject/       # Project settings
│   ├── settings.py
│   ├── urls.py
│   └── wsgi.py
├── blog/            # App 1
│   ├── models.py
│   ├── views.py
│   └── urls.py
└── users/           # App 2
    ├── models.py
    ├── views.py
    └── urls.py
```

## Creating an App

```bash
python manage.py startapp blog
```

## App Structure

```
blog/
├── __init__.py
├── admin.py      # Admin configuration
├── apps.py       # App configuration
├── models.py     # Database models
├── tests.py      # Unit tests
├── views.py      # View functions/classes
└── migrations/   # Database migrations
```

## Register App in settings.py

```python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'django.contrib.admin',
    'django.contrib.auth',
    # ... other apps
    'blog',  # Add your app here!
]
```

slides.title: MTV Architecture
slides.content:
# Model-Template-View (MTV) 🏗️ Django follows the MTV pattern, similar to MVC. ## The MTV Flow ``` 1. User requests URL → 2. URL routes to View → 3. View fetches Model data → 4. View renders Template → 5. Response sent to user ``` ## Model (M) Defines your data structure. ```python # models.py from django.db import models class Article(models.Model): title = models.CharField(max_length=200) content = models.TextField() published = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True) ``` ## Template (T) HTML with Django template language. ```html

{{ article.title }}

{{ article.content }}

``` ## View (V) Business logic - connects Model and Template. ```python # views.py from django.shortcuts import render from .models import Article def article_detail(request, pk): article = Article.objects.get(pk=pk) return render(request, 'article.html', {'article': article}) ``` > 💡 **MTV vs MVC:** Django's "View" is like MVC's "Controller", and Django's "Template" is like MVC's "View".

slides.title: Key Files Explained
slides.content:
# Important Django Files 📄

## manage.py

Command-line utility for administrative tasks.

```bash
python manage.py runserver      # Run dev server
python manage.py migrate         # Apply migrations
python manage.py createsuperuser # Create admin user
python manage.py shell           # Python shell with Django
```

## settings.py

All project configuration.

```python
# Key settings
DEBUG = True                    # Development mode
ALLOWED_HOSTS = []              # Allowed domains
INSTALLED_APPS = [...]          # Registered apps
DATABASES = {...}               # Database config
STATIC_URL = '/static/'         # Static files
TEMPLATES = [...]               # Template config
```

## urls.py

URL routing configuration.

```python
from django.urls import path, include

urlpatterns = [
    path('admin/', admin.site.urls),
    path('blog/', include('blog.urls')),
]
```

## wsgi.py / asgi.py

Entry points for WSGI/ASGI servers.

```python
# For production deployment
application = get_wsgi_application()
```

> 💡 **WSGI** = Web Server Gateway Interface (synchronous)
> **ASGI** = Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface (async support)

slides.title: Your First Django App
slides.content:
# Quick Start: Hello Django! 👋 ## Step 1: Create View ```python # blog/views.py from django.http import HttpResponse def home(request): return HttpResponse("

Hello, Django!

") ``` ## Step 2: Create URL Route ```python # blog/urls.py from django.urls import path from . import views urlpatterns = [ path('', views.home, name='home'), ] ``` ## Step 3: Include in Project URLs ```python # myproject/urls.py from django.urls import path, include urlpatterns = [ path('admin/', admin.site.urls), path('', include('blog.urls')), ] ``` ## Step 4: Run and Visit ```bash python manage.py runserver # Visit http://127.0.0.1:8000/ # See "Hello, Django!" 🎉 ``` ## Django Development Cycle ``` 1. Edit code 2. Server auto-reloads 3. Refresh browser 4. See changes instantly! ``` > 🎯 **Congrats!** You've built your first Django view!
